subject: english
topic: Oral English: word stress (choose the word with the correct stress pattern, stressed syllable in CAPITALS)

kept.q: In Nigerian secondary schools, students are often tested on the stress pattern of the word PRESENT, which can function as either a noun or a verb. Choose the option that shows the CORRECT stress pattern when PRESENT means a gift given to someone.
kept.explanation: When PRESENT is used as a noun meaning a gift, the stress falls on the first syllable. If it were used as a verb meaning to give or show something, the stress would shift to the second syllable instead.
kept.pidgin: If you wan talk say person give you gift, you go stress the first part of the word. But if you wan talk say you dey show person something, the stress go move go the second part.

kept.q: Four WAEC examiners disagreed on how to stress the word NECESSARY during a marking workshop. Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
kept.explanation: NECESSARY is stressed on the first syllable, even though it has four syllables. Many candidates wrongly place stress on the second syllable because of the strong middle sound, but standard pronunciation keeps the stress at the front.
kept.pidgin: For this word, the correct stress dey for the first syllable. Many people dey make mistake put am for the middle, but that one no correct.

kept.q: The word INCREASE can be used as both a noun and a verb in English, and its stress pattern changes with its grammatical function. Choose the option with the CORRECT stress pattern for INCREASE when it functions as a verb meaning to become greater.
kept.explanation: As a verb, INCREASE is stressed on the second syllable, while as a noun it is stressed on the first syllable. This noun-verb stress shift is common in many two-syllable English words such as CONTRACT and RECORD.
kept.pidgin: When you use this word as verb, the stress must dey for the second syllable. If na noun you dey use, the stress go come back for the first one.

q.q: Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
q.explanation: The noun PHOTOGRAPH is stressed on the first syllable. This is different from PHOTOGRAPHY, which shifts stress to the second syllable, so candidates must not confuse the two forms.

q.q: The word MANAGEMENT is written below in four different stress patterns, with the stressed syllable in CAPITALS. Choose the option with the correct stress pattern.
q.explanation: MANAGEMENT is a three-syllable noun stressed on the first syllable. English nouns of this type commonly take first-syllable stress, unlike words ending in -tion or -ity.

q.q: Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
q.explanation: ECONOMIC is stressed on the third syllable, unlike its related word ECONOMY, which is stressed on the second syllable. This shift happens because the suffix -ic often pulls stress toward itself.

q.q: Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
q.explanation: REFEREE is a three-syllable word stressed on the final syllable. Words ending in -ee, such as EMPLOYEE and TRAINEE, usually carry stress on that last syllable.

q.q: Four candidates pronounced the word CONTRIBUTE differently in a mock oral test at a school in Enugu. Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
q.explanation: CONTRIBUTE is a verb stressed on the second syllable. Many learners wrongly stress the first syllable, perhaps influenced by related nouns like CONTRIBUTION.
